comments.body:
RCA (debug-protocol Phase 1, analysis-only) — root cause PROVEN by local stubbed-transport experiments (no Jira). IMPORTANT CONTEXT FIRST: the production fix has ALREADY LANDED on origin/main as commit 30c522cde9 under [rebar:ab7f-f0cc-7384-43a7] (closed), whose message states 'Closes the production half of cabc-7a98-d173-4d7c'. This ticket therefore looks ready for verification + close by its owner; evidence below.

CONFIRMED ROOT CAUSE (pre-fix tree = parent of 30c522cde9). All three whole-project readers in src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/acli_graph.py — get_parent_map (loop at :218), get_comment_map (:319), get_issuelinks_map (:413, pre-fix line numbers) — walked POST /rest/api/3/search/jql with a hand-rolled cursor loop whose ONLY exits were 'isLast' truthy or a null/absent 'nextPageToken'. No same-token-twice guard and no request ceiling: a server that repeats the same non-null nextPageToken with isLast falsy makes every request byte-identical, neither break fires, and the loop never terminates. Second-order defect: each loop's fail-open 'except Exception: log WARNING; break' converts the eventual transport failure into a silently PARTIAL whole-project map — the same silent-truncation class as change 1105, [rebar:9263-b404-cb6c-463f], [rebar:deac-4f5a-856a-49bd]. The guard already existed in fetcher._iter_pages (fetcher.py:293-306, SilentTruncationError reason='same-token-twice'); these readers are a separate cursor path and lacked it.

DISCRIMINATING EVIDENCE (runtime, _direct_rest_post_json stubbed):
- E1, pre-fix readers vs a stub returning {issues:[1 issue], nextPageToken:'same-token-forever'}: each of the 3 readers issued 26 requests, stopped ONLY by the harness cap at 25, swallowed the harness error at WARNING ('REST search failed ... degrading gracefully'), and RETURNED a 1-entry map — reproduces this ticket's measurement exactly (26 requests, 1-entry map).
- E2 kills the rival hypothesis 'the client fails to echo the cursor, so the server legitimately repeats': recorded bodies show request 1 carries no token and requests 2+ all echo nextPageToken='same-token-forever' byte-identically. The echo is correct; the defect is purely the missing stall guard.
- E3 proves the changeable artifact: HEAD readers against the SAME stub stop at exactly 2 requests and raise RunawayPaginationError PAST the fail-open handler (nothing swallowed). Same server, one variable — the guard — flips the behavior as predicted.
- E4: held-out suite green on HEAD: 42 passed in tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_acli_graph_pagination_heldout.py, including test_a_repeated_cursor_token_stops_the_walk_on_its_own, now a plain assertion (:367).

LEGITIMACY: defect — behavior violated the pre-existing strict-xfail oracle and the design invariant already enforced in fetcher._iter_pages, with three prior closed bugs in the same class.

AC STATUS ON HEAD (all four met): (1) all three readers route through the single shared _iter_cursor_pages (acli_graph.py:41-88). (2) a stalled cursor is LOUD — it raises the dedicated RunawayPaginationError (acli_graph.py:80-86) rather than fetcher's SilentTruncationError(reason='same-token-twice'); intent (loud, no partial map) is met and a distinct exception for the distinct cursor protocol is defensible — recording that deviation here since the AC named the fetcher exception. (3) the fail-open handlers no longer convert a stall into a partial map: explicit 'except RunawayPaginationError: raise' arms at acli_graph.py:304-307, :394-397, :477-480. (4) the xfail is converted to a plain passing assertion.

SIBLING CANDIDATES across the other paginated readers (named, not filed):
- jira_datacenter/transport.py::_paged_search (:379-416) — CONFIRMED at runtime as a live sibling of the class: it terminates ONLY on an empty batch (:412) with no repeated-page/offset-stall guard, so a DC server that ignores startAt and re-serves the same non-empty page spins forever — my stub probe issued 26 calls and ended only at the 25-call harness cap, exactly like pre-fix acli_graph. fetcher._iter_pages carries offset-stall detection for precisely this; DC's pager does not, and test_dc_transport_pagination_heldout.py has NO stall/runaway coverage (no offset-stall / same-token / runaway hits). Second-order twin: DC get_parent_map (:515) wraps it in 'except Exception' (:547) returning {} silently; get_issuelinks_map (:418) and get_comment_map (:432) call it unwrapped. Note [rebar:ab7f-f0cc-7384-43a7] deliberately scoped this pager OUT as stable and pinned by bug 9263's structural gate — but that pin covers short-page/advance-by-returned semantics, not a stall guard; the stall hole is real and unpinned.
- fetcher.py::_iter_pages (:288) — clean; it is the reference implementation (same-token-twice + offset-stall guards).
- adapters/jira/acli_cli_ops.py::_parse_paginated_comments (:517) / get_comments --paginate — not a rebar-driven cursor loop (pagination happens inside the ACLI binary; the parser iterates a finite string). No spin risk in rebar code.

PHASE-2 SKETCH: for THIS ticket no production work remains — verify 30c522cde9 against the ACs (done above) and close referencing ab7f. The regression RED oracle already exists and has teeth: removing the token-equality guard at acli_graph.py:80 sends test_a_repeated_cursor_token_stops_the_walk_on_its_own red (E1 vs E3 demonstrated exactly that flip). For the DC sibling, if picked up: add a stall guard inside _paged_search mirroring fetcher._iter_pages semantics (repeated FULL page = raise a loud stall error; repeated SHORT page = clean stop), and the suggested RED oracle is a test in test_dc_transport_pagination_heldout.py driving _paged_search with a startAt-ignoring stub client, asserting it self-terminates within 2 calls with a loud error instead of hitting a harness call cap.

compiled_state.description:
# Cloud's acli_graph whole-project readers spin forever on a repeated cursor token

## Mechanism (proven, not inferred)

`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/acli_graph.py` — all three whole-project
readers (`get_parent_map` :215-278, `get_comment_map` :318-376, `get_issuelinks_map`
:412-473) walk `POST /rest/api/3/search/jql` with this loop shape:

    while True:
        ... resp = self._direct_rest_post_json("/rest/api/3/search/jql", body)
        if resp.get("isLast"): break
        next_page_token = resp.get("nextPageToken")
        if not next_page_token: break

If the server returns the SAME non-null `nextPageToken` on consecutive responses with
`isLast` falsy, the request body is byte-identical each iteration, the response is
identical, and neither break fires: the loop never terminates. There is no
same-token-twice guard and no request-count ceiling.

`fetcher._iter_pages` has exactly this guard (`fetcher.py:286-308`, `token_seen_count` ->
`SilentTruncationError(reason="same-token-twice")`); these three readers, a separate code
path with a separate cursor, do not.

Second-order effect: because each reader wraps the POST in a fail-open
`except Exception: ... break`, the spin ends only when the transport itself finally
errors, and that error is then swallowed at WARNING — so the pass completes with a
SILENTLY PARTIAL map (missing parents / comments / links), which is the same invisible
symptom as the truncation bugs in change 1105, [rebar:9263-b404-cb6c-463f] and
[rebar:deac-4f5a-856a-49bd].

## Reproduction

Substitute `_direct_rest_post_json` with a stub returning
`{"issues": [...], "nextPageToken": "same-token-forever"}` (no `isLast`). Measured on
this branch: 26 requests issued, ending only because the harness raised at its own
25-call cap; result was a 1-entry map. Without the harness cap the call does not return.

The oracle for the fixed behaviour already exists, as a strict xfail:
`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_acli_graph_pagination_heldout.py`
`::test_a_repeated_cursor_token_stops_the_walk_on_its_own`. It asserts the reader stops
on its own within two requests. When the guard lands the xfail turns strict-red and must
be converted to a plain assertion.

## Why it was not fixed under 0fad

0fad is a test-parity ticket (its ACs are tests + a structural guard); its instructions
scoped production changes out. This ticket carries the production fix.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] the three `acli_graph` readers stop on a repeated cursor token instead of spinning
      — preferably by routing all three through one shared cursor pager rather than a
      fourth hand-rolled loop
- [ ] a stalled cursor is LOUD, matching `fetcher._iter_pages`: raise
      `SilentTruncationError(reason="same-token-twice")` rather than returning a partial
      map, or state on this ticket why a silent stop is correct for these readers
- [ ] the fail-open `except Exception` no longer converts a stalled cursor into a silently
      partial whole-project map
- [ ] `test_a_repeated_cursor_token_stops_the_walk_on_its_own` is converted from
      `xfail(strict=True)` to a plain passing assertion
